using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

namespace Avowry.Compiler.Tests.Diagnostics;

/// <summary>
/// Loads the 19 trigger sources and their pre-change diagnostic rows, and maps
/// the 13 adopted new fragments back to the old wording (and the reverse).
/// </summary>
internal static class TriggerSources
{
    private static readonly (string Old, string New)[] Fragments =
    [
        ("Phrase '", "Avow '"),
        ("Phrase specs cannot", "Avow specs cannot"),
        ("Phrase spec for '", "Avow spec for '"),
        ("Phrase has no implementation", "Avow has no implementation"),
        ("Composite phrase '", "Composite avow '"),
        (" on phrase '", " on avow '"),
        ("for a phrase that returns", "for an avow that returns"),
        ("No phrase matches", "No avow matches"),
        ("A phrase is implemented", "An avow is implemented"),
        ("a quoted phrase template", "a quoted avow template"),
        ("a phrase clause", "an avow clause"),
        ("a phrase call", "an avow call"),
        ("(phrase spec)", "(avow spec)"),
    ];

    private static readonly Dictionary<string, string> NewToOld =
        Fragments.ToDictionary(pair => pair.New, pair => pair.Old, StringComparer.Ordinal);

    private static readonly Dictionary<string, string> OldToNew =
        Fragments.ToDictionary(pair => pair.Old, pair => pair.New, StringComparer.Ordinal);

    private static readonly Regex NewFragments = Alternation(Fragments.Select(pair => pair.New));
    private static readonly Regex OldFragments = Alternation(Fragments.Select(pair => pair.Old));

    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> SourceById;
    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyList<BaselineRow>> BaselineById;

    static TriggerSources()
    {
        var directory = DiagnosticsDirectory();
        SourceById = ParseSources(ReadLf(Path.Combine(directory, "sources.txt")));
        BaselineById = ParseBaseline(ReadLf(Path.Combine(directory, "baseline.txt")));
        Ids = [.. SourceById.Keys];
    }

    public static IReadOnlyList<string> Ids { get; }

    public static string Source(string id) => SourceById[id];

    public static IReadOnlyList<BaselineRow> Baseline(string id) => BaselineById[id];

    public static IEnumerable<string> BaselineTexts() =>
        Ids.SelectMany(Baseline).Select(row => row.Text);

    public static string ToOld(string text) =>
        NewFragments.Replace(text, match => NewToOld[match.Value]);

    public static string ToNew(string text) =>
        OldFragments.Replace(text, match => OldToNew[match.Value]);

    internal sealed record BaselineRow(string Code, int Line, int Column, string Text)
    {
        public string LineText => $"{Code}|{Line}|{Column}|{Text}";
    }

    private static Regex Alternation(IEnumerable<string> fragments)
    {
        var escaped = fragments
            .OrderByDescending(fragment => fragment.Length)
            .Select(Regex.Escape);
        return new Regex(string.Join("|", escaped), RegexOptions.CultureInvariant);
    }

    private static string DiagnosticsDirectory()
    {
        for (var dir = new DirectoryInfo(AppContext.BaseDirectory); dir is not null; dir = dir.Parent)
        {
            if (File.Exists(Path.Combine(dir.FullName, "Avowry.sln")))
                return Path.Combine(dir.FullName, "tests", "Avowry.Compiler.Tests", "Diagnostics");
        }

        throw new DirectoryNotFoundException("Could not find Avowry.sln above the test output directory.");
    }

    private static string ReadLf(string path) =>
        File.ReadAllText(path).Replace("\r\n", "\n", StringComparison.Ordinal).Replace('\r', '\n');

    private static Dictionary<string, string> ParseSources(string text)
    {
        var sources = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        foreach (var block in text.Split("### ", StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries))
        {
            var (id, body) = SplitId(block);
            sources.Add(id, body.TrimEnd('\n'));
        }

        return sources;
    }

    private static Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyList<BaselineRow>> ParseBaseline(string text)
    {
        var baselines = new Dictionary<string, IReadOnlyList<BaselineRow>>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
        foreach (var block in text.Split("### ", StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries))
        {
            var (id, body) = SplitId(block);
            var rows = new List<BaselineRow>();
            foreach (var line in body.Split('\n'))
            {
                if (!line.StartsWith("PH", StringComparison.Ordinal))
                    continue;
                var parts = line.Split('|', 4);
                rows.Add(new BaselineRow(parts[0], int.Parse(parts[1]), int.Parse(parts[2]), parts[3]));
            }

            baselines.Add(id, rows);
        }

        return baselines;
    }

    private static (string Id, string Body) SplitId(string block)
    {
        var end = block.IndexOf('\n');
        var id = (end < 0 ? block : block[..end]).Trim();
        var body = end < 0 ? "" : block[(end + 1)..];
        return (id, body);
    }
}

using Avowry.Compiler.Semantics;

namespace Avowry.Compiler.Tests.Diagnostics;

// Feature: Diagnostic characterisation (card 324 criterion 2)
//   Every recorded trigger keeps its diagnostic code, position and tail; only the
//   unit word may change, and only through the adopted a/an fragments.
public class DiagnosticCharacterisationTests
{
    public static TheoryData<string> SourceIds()
    {
        var data = new TheoryData<string>();
        foreach (var id in TriggerSources.Ids)
            data.Add(id);
        return data;
    }

    [Theory]
    [Trait("Criterion", "2")]
    [MemberData(nameof(SourceIds))]
    public void Diagnostic_codes_positions_and_tails_are_unchanged(string id)
    {
        // Given a trigger source whose diagnostics are recorded in the baseline
        var source = TriggerSources.Source(id);

        // When it is compiled
        var actual = Resolver.Resolve(source).Diagnostics
            .Select(diagnostic => $"{diagnostic.Code}|{diagnostic.Line}|{diagnostic.Column}|{TriggerSources.ToOld(diagnostic.Message)}")
            .ToList();

        // Then the whole list matches the baseline rows after ToOld
        var expected = TriggerSources.Baseline(id).Select(row => row.LineText).ToList();
        Assert.Equal(expected, actual);
    }

    [Fact]
    [Trait("Criterion", "2")]
    public void The_baseline_covers_every_source_and_each_source_triggers()
    {
        // Given the recorded trigger sources
        var ids = TriggerSources.Ids;

        // When each source is compiled
        // Then there are 19 ids, each with a baseline row, and each yields a diagnostic
        Assert.Equal(19, ids.Count);
        foreach (var id in ids)
        {
            Assert.NotEmpty(TriggerSources.Baseline(id));
            Assert.NotEmpty(Resolver.Resolve(TriggerSources.Source(id)).Diagnostics);
        }
    }

    [Fact]
    [Trait("Criterion", "2")]
    public void Normalisation_does_not_hide_wording_drift()
    {
        // Given nine wording drifts that are not the adopted new fragments
        string[] samples =
        [
            "Avow  'ping {m: Int}' has the same wording as 'ping {n: Int}'.",
            "an avow 'count things' returns Int; use 'let' to keep it.",
            "Expected a avow clause (effects, fails with, spec, native or steps), found 'returns'.",
            "No avows match this step. Closest: \"do nothing\".",
            "Composite Avow 'count {n: Int}' cannot return a value.",
            "Avow' ping {m: Int}' has the same wording as 'ping {n: Int}'.",
            "avow 'do nothing' returns no value and cannot be used with 'let'.",
            "Phrase 'not-a-trigger' has drifted.",
            "An avow  is implemented by native blocks or by steps, not both.",
        ];
        var oldTexts = TriggerSources.BaselineTexts().ToHashSet(StringComparer.Ordinal);

        // When each drift is run through ToOld
        // Then none equals a legitimate baseline old text
        foreach (var sample in samples)
            Assert.False(oldTexts.Contains(TriggerSources.ToOld(sample)), sample);
    }
}

# Coding guidelines for this repository

These rules cover the code of this repository: the compiler, the adapters, the command line tool, the scripts and the tests. They are different from the project-profile coding standards that Avowry applies to the code it generates for users (see `docs/adr/ADR-library-binding-layering.md`); that profile describes the output, this file describes the tool that makes it. Reviewers check every change against this file.

Principle for every rule below: a reader, human or a fresh-context seat, should be able to understand and change one thing by reading only that thing. The rules exist to keep each unit cohesive, its dependencies few and pointing one way, and its behaviour pinned by a test that can fail.

## Design

- **High cohesion, low coupling.** A unit (function, type, file, document) has one reason to change. If describing it needs the word "and", split it. Why: small cohesive units are cheap to read, test and revert.
- **Dependencies point one way.** Lower layers never know about higher ones. The order is lexer, parser, resolver and model, target adapter, command line, tooling. A lower layer exposes data or an interface it owns; a higher layer plugs in. The generated code is the lowest layer of all and must not know about the compiler that produced it or the tools that trace it (Decider D111). Why: an inverted dependency makes the low-level artifact change whenever the tooling changes.
- **Small functions.** Aim for about 20 lines; past 30 is a sign of several responsibilities. Prefer at most two parameters; when more values travel together, name them as a record. Why: short functions are testable one behaviour at a time.
- **No flag parameters.** A boolean that switches behaviour is two functions. A function either computes and returns, or performs an action, not both. Why: callers read the call site, not the body.
- **Immutable data.** Syntax trees, models and diagnostics are records that are never mutated after construction; build a new value instead. Why: stages stay independent and results are reproducible.
- **Separate policy from mechanism.** Choices that vary by target, library or environment live in an adapter or an option, not in the core.

## Naming

- Functions and methods are verbs for one action; types are nouns; booleans read as predicates (`IsDeclared`, `HasFailure`). Avoid `Manager`, `Helper`, `Util` and `Data` as names: they hide the responsibility.
- No abbreviations except universally known ones (`id`, `url`). Diagnostics keep the existing `PHnnn` code style, one code per distinct problem.
- A name states what a thing is or does, not how it is used today.

## Errors and determinism

- **The compiler never throws on user input.** A bad or hostile source file produces a diagnostic with a code and a location, not an exception. Exceptions are for programmer errors only. Why: a tool that crashes teaches nothing and hides the real problem.
- **Output is deterministic and portable.** The same source gives the same bytes on Windows and Linux and from any working directory: no timestamps, no absolute paths, no culture-dependent formatting, no dependence on line endings or file ordering. CI runs on Linux, so a test that only passes on one platform is a defect.
- **Fail loudly at boundaries, trust inside.** Validate at the edge (files, arguments, model replies); inside, rely on the types.

## Tests

- **Test first.** Watch the test fail for the right reason before writing the code; a red that survives when only the fix is reverted proves the test measures the change.
- **A test must be able to fail.** Before accepting a test, name the change that would break it, and check it when the check is cheap. Assertions that cannot fail (a check on something that cannot contain the value, a count that is never zero, a regex that matches anything) are deleted or replaced. Why: a test that cannot fail is false assurance.
- **Name the behaviour.** A test name is a sentence about observable behaviour (`Unknown_field_in_an_update_reports_a_diagnostic`), not the method under test. One behaviour per test.
- **Given, When, Then comments** mark the three parts; the setup, the single action and the observable result. Cover zero, one, many, boundaries, interface and exception paths for each behaviour.
- **Assert the exact result.** Prefer the full expected value over a pattern; when a pattern is needed, anchor it.
- **Keep tests independent and fast.** No ordering between tests, no sleeps, no shared mutable state, no network. Use fakes for time, processes and models. Nested tool runs stay disabled for node reuse and are stopped by exact process id.
- **Traits tie a test to its card** (`Slice`), so the card's check can count them.

## Code hygiene

- **No dead code.** Delete unused code, commented-out code and stale options; history keeps them. Why: unread code misleads the next reader.
- **No hidden coupling through strings.** Shared names (keywords, diagnostic codes, failure names) have one definition that others reference.
- **Leave touched files cleaner, in scope.** Rename a poor name, extract a helper, remove dead code in the files a change touches. Code that a change impacts is part of the change: fix a test the change turns red, do not hand it to someone else.
- **Small, atomic, revertable commits.** One concern per commit and per card, so any decision can be undone cleanly. Stage explicit paths only.
- **Comments say why**, never what; the code says what. A comment that repeats the code is deleted.

## Documents

- One concern per document; a reader loads only what they need. Cross-references are links, not copies.
- State a direction as a principle with its rationale, never as who asked for it; use the role "the product owner" where an owner must be named.
- Generated files carry no knowledge of the layers above them.

## Review checklist

A reviewer confirms, for the change in front of them (the item numbers are stable; add new ones at the end):

1. Each new unit has one responsibility and a name that says it; no function over about 30 lines without a reason.
2. Dependencies point downward; nothing low-level learned about something above it.
3. Bad input produces diagnostics, never an exception.
4. Output is deterministic on Windows and Linux.
5. Every new test could fail: the reviewer can name the breaking change; no assertion is vacuous.
6. Test names describe behaviour; Given, When, Then comments are present; edge and failure paths are covered.
7. No dead code, no commented-out code, no duplicated shared names.
8. The change is small enough to revert alone; unrelated cleanup is not mixed in.
9. Documents touched hold one concern, link instead of copying, and give rationale.
10. For an emitter or adapter change, the generated output is identical to before unless the card says otherwise: the recorded output hashes are unchanged, and any change is named exactly and justified in the card.
11. The full gate was run alone and CI on Linux is green.

+using Avowry.Compiler.Semantics;
+
+namespace Avowry.Compiler.Tests.Diagnostics;

+    public void The_eight_leading_messages_say_Avow(string id, string expected)

+        // Given a trigger source and the first diagnostic recorded for it
+        var source = TriggerSources.Source(id);
+        var baseline = TriggerSources.Baseline(id)[0];
+
+        // When it is compiled
+        var actual = Resolver.Resolve(source).Diagnostics.Single(diagnostic =>
+            diagnostic.Code == baseline.Code &&
+            diagnostic.Line == baseline.Line &&
+            diagnostic.Column == baseline.Column);
+
+        // Then its identity is unchanged and its full message names the avow

+        Assert.Equal(baseline.Line, actual.Line);
+        Assert.Equal(baseline.Column, actual.Column);
+        Assert.Equal(expected, actual.Message);
+    }
